importantNotes: Joshua's name (Yehoshua) means 'The LORD saves' — same root as Jesus (Yeshua).
Rahab's faith saved her family — she is in the lineage of Christ (Matt 1:5).
The fall of Jericho teaches that God's battles are won His way, not ours.
'Choose this day whom you will serve' (24:15) remains a powerful call to commitment.
Not one of God's promises failed — every one was fulfilled (21:45).

chapters.1: God commissions Joshua to lead Israel into the Promised Land with courage.
chapters.2: Joshua sends two spies to Jericho; Rahab hides them and is promised safety.
chapters.3: Israel crosses the Jordan River on dry ground as the priests carry the Ark.
chapters.4: Twelve memorial stones are set up to commemorate the Jordan crossing.
chapters.5: Circumcision at Gilgal; the manna ceases; Joshua encounters the Commander of the LORD's army.
chapters.6: The walls of Jericho fall after Israel marches around the city for seven days.
chapters.7: Achan's sin causes Israel's defeat at Ai; he is punished.
chapters.8: Israel conquers Ai using an ambush strategy; the law is read on Mount Ebal.
chapters.9: The Gibeonites deceive Israel into making a treaty with them.
chapters.10: The sun stands still during battle; Joshua defeats the southern Canaanite kings.
chapters.11: Joshua defeats the northern kings and conquers much of the land.
chapters.12: A list of the kings defeated by Moses and Joshua.
chapters.13: Land still to be conquered; territory assigned to Reuben, Gad, and half-Manasseh.
chapters.14: Caleb receives Hebron as his inheritance because he followed God wholeheartedly.
chapters.15: The territory allotted to the tribe of Judah.
chapters.16: The territory allotted to the tribe of Ephraim.
chapters.17: The territory allotted to the half-tribe of Manasseh west of the Jordan.
chapters.18: The Tabernacle is set up at Shiloh; territory allotted to Benjamin.
chapters.19: Territories allotted to Simeon, Zebulun, Issachar, Asher, Naphtali, and Dan.
chapters.20: Six cities of refuge are designated for those who accidentally kill someone.
chapters.21: Forty-eight cities are given to the Levites from the other tribes' territories.
chapters.22: The eastern tribes build an altar; a potential conflict is resolved peacefully.
chapters.23: Joshua's farewell speech — remain faithful to God and avoid intermarriage with pagans.
chapters.24: Joshua renews the covenant at Shechem; 'as for me and my house, we will serve the LORD.'
